HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06762

Full Title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A FRAMEWORK FOR BLUE ECONOMY, PROMOTING STEWARDSHIP AND SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT OF COASTAL AND MARINE ECOSYSTEMS AND RESOURCES



Short Title: Blue Economy Act



Abstract: Seeks to protect the Philippines' marine wealth while enhancing its potential for sustainable development, food security, and climate resilience. Creates the Blue Economy Council that shall formulate, oversee, and coordinate the country’s integrated blue economy strategy. Creates the Blue Economic Zone (BEZs) to support ocean-based industries. Promotes “Blue Carbon” and standardizes blue financial instruments like bonds and securities to fund sustainable projects. Provides tax exemptions, duty-free importations, and access to credit guarantees to registered enterprises in the blue economy. Mandates the Local Government Units (LGUs) to retain jurisdiction over municipal waters but are required to act as frontline agencies in implementing the IMCAM framework and developing local maritime spatial plans aligned with the national strategy.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB05019

Full Title: AN ACT ALLOWING THE APPOINTMENT OF FACULTY, RESEARCHERS, AND ADMINISTRATORS WITH DUAL CITIZENSHIP IN PUBLIC HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 5 (3) OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9225, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE "CITIZENSHIP RETENTION AND RE-ACQUISITION ACT OF 2003"

Short Title: Allowing The Appointment Of Faculty, Researchers, And Administrators With Dual Citizenship In Public Higher Education Institutions, Amending Section 5 (3) Of Republic Act No. 9225

Abstract: Seeks to allow qualified professional with dual citizenship to work as faculty members in the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), either on a full time or part time basis, without renouncing their foreign citizenship before they could teach to provide the public HEIs a wider elbow room to hire individuals who possesses skills and qualifications needed for their institutions.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06276

Full Title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A LOAN RESTRUCTURING AND CONDONATION PROGRAM FOR SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING

Short Title: Housing Loan Condonation Act

Abstract: Aims to make available at affordable cost, decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens. Condones all socialized and low-cost housing loans with the NHA, SHFC, NHMFC, AND PCG that have at least three (3) months of unpaid monthly amortizations for a period of twenty-four (24) months after the issuance of the implementing rules and regulations of this Act, provided, that the original principal amount of the housing loans shall not exceed One million eight hundred thousand pesos (P1,800,00.00). Authorizes the NHA, SHFC, NHMFC, and PGC to continue the loan restructuring and condonation program notwithstanding the lapse of twenty-four months application period. Allows restructuring of housing loans and the assumption of payment of outstanding loan by the legal heirs and successors-in-interest. Provides incentives to all accounts which monthly amortization are paid on time.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09048

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHT OF GOVERNMENT TO EXPROPRIATE LANDS FOR SOCIALIZED HOUSING, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTIONS 9, 10, AND 11 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7279, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE URBAN DEVELOPMENT AND HOUSING ACT OF 1992

Short Title: Strengthening The Right Of Government To Expropriate Lands For Socialized Housing, Amending For The Purpose Sections 9, 10, And 11 Of Republic Act No. 7279, Otherwise Known As The Urban Development And Housing Act Of 1992

Abstract: Aims to enhance the government’s power to expropriate various types of land – government –owned, alienable public lands, abandoned, idle, and privately owned – specifically for socialized housing projects. It seeks to streamline land acquisition processes, clarify priorities, and ensure lawful, efficient expropriation procedures in coordination with relevant agencies. Removes the previous mandatory priority order for land acquisition, allowing the government to acquire any suitable lands, alienable public lands, unregistered or abandoned lands, areas within priority development zones, BLISS sites, and privately owned lands. It emphasizes that on-site development on government lands should be prioritized and that land identification and prioritization are to be coordinated with the Department of Human Settlements and Urban Development. Stipulates that expropriation should be resorted to only after exhausting other modes, with specific provisions excluding small property owners and pending litigation from exemption. Expropriation proceedings shall follow the procedure laid down under Rule 67 of the Rules of Courts and Section 19 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991, as amended.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06739

Full Title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE DR. EVA MACARAEG-MACAPAGAL NATIONAL CENTER FOR GERIATRIC HEALTH UNDER THE JOSE R. REYES MEMORIAL MEDICAL CENTER AS THE DR. EVA MACARAEG-MACAPAGAL NATIONAL CENTER FOR GERIATRIC HEALTH AND RESEARCH INSTITUTE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Geriatric Health Act

Abstract: Aims to protect and promote the right to health of senior citizens by ensuring holistic health services through the establishment of a geriatric specialty hospital and research institute. Grants the Dr. Eva Macaraeg-Macapagal National Center for Geriatric Health and Research Institute (DEMM-NCGHRI) the function to serve as an apex hospital or end-referral facility which shall specialize in geriatric health services; provide higher and up-to-date geriatric training for professionals, postgraduates, academics and allied healthcare providers especially from the geriatric specialty centers and; conduct cutting edge research studies on diseases related to old age for the development of policies, protocols, standards, and solutions for specialized health care, among others. Provides tax exemptions for all donations, endowments, contributions, grants and bequests used actually, directly and exclusively for and in accordance with the purposes and functions of the DEMM-NCGHRI. Mandates the DEMM-NCGHRI to submit an annual report to the President of the Philippines, the Senate Committee on Health and Demography, and the House of Representatives Committee on Health, on its activities, accomplishments, and recommendations.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06789

Full Title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES AND THE WATER REGULATORY COMMISSION, DEFINING THEIR MANDATES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: National Water Resources Management Act

Abstract: Aims to ensure universal access to safe, affordable, and sustainable water while addressing the challenges of climate change and ecological balance. Creates the Department of Water Resources (DWR) which shall be the primary agency responsible for the comprehensive and integrated identification and mapping of all water resources, planning, policy formulation, and management of the ownership, appropriation, utilization, exploitation, development, and protection of water resources in the Philippines to ensure optimal use thereof. Establishes the Water Regulatory Commission which shall cover and apply to all service providers, whether private or public, providing or intending to provide water supply, including suppliers to subdivisions or other service providers, sewerage, or septage treatment and disposal services for domestic, residential, institutional, industrial or commercial use. Establishes interdepartmental relations with other agencies such as the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Health (DOH), LGUs and the PCC. Promotes “water demand management” as a national policy, encouraging recycling, rainwater harvesting, and efficient pricing to make conservation a way of life. Mandates that a portion (up to 10%) of proceeds from raw water extraction be shared with the Local Government Units (LGUs) or Indigenous Cultural Communities (IPs) that own the land where the water is sourced. Provides the Department and Commission to absorb the relevant functions and rights of existing agencies, such as the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) and the regulatory units of the MWSS and LWUA.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB07628

Full Title: AN ACT MANDATING THE INCLUSION OF A PERSONAL FINANCIAL LITERACY COURSE IN THE TERTIARY EDUCATION CURRICULUM OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS, TECHNICAL-VOCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND SKILLS DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY TRAINING CENTERS

Short Title: Personal Financial Literacy Course In The Tertiary Education Curriculum Act

Abstract: Seeks to ensure that technical-vocational institutions (TVIs) and Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) training centers shall provide the necessary financial education and literacy to technical-vocational (tech-voc) students to help them learn and develop the appropriate skills to make well-informed financial decisions, and desirable work habits upon employment in the industries.

Significance: NATIONAL

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08043

Full Title: AN ACT REDUCING FOOD SURPLUS THROUGH FOOD DONATIONS AND FOOD WASTE RECYCLING

Short Title: Food Waste Reduction And Prevention Act

Abstract: Aims to attain food security, end hunger, promote the efficient use of the country’s food resources, and protect the environment by reducing food waste and its greenhouse gas emissions. Mandates the donation of edible food surplus to accredited food banks. Requires covered establishments to implement food waste prevention plans, reduce surplus at source, and enter into contracts with food banks. Businesses achieving at least 20% reduction in edible surplus are eligible for enhanced tax deductions.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08420

Full Title: AN ACT DEFINING TECHNOLOGY-FACILITATED VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN, PROVIDING PROTECTIVE MEASURES, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9262, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN ACT OF 2004”

Short Title: Expanded Anti - Violence Against Women And Their Children ( E - V A W C ) Act

Abstract: Seeks to define and address electronic violence against women and their children. Broadens the scope to include acts committed or condoned by the state, covering physical, sexual, psychological, and economic abuse. Psychological violence includes coercion to witness abuse, pornography, harm to pets, or deprivation of custody or visitation rights. Defines acts involving data, ICT devices, or digital media causing mental, emotional, sexual, or physical harm. Includes unauthorized recording/distribution of intimate images or videos, cyber harassment, stalking, fake news creation, and malicious social media account use. Imposes penalties of reclusion temporal, fines between P300,000.00 to P500,000.00 and mandatory psychological or psychiatric treatment. Provides Family or Regional Trial Courts the exclusive jurisdiction over VAWC cases. Cases involving technology-facilitated violence against women and their children (TFVAWC) can be filed where the offense occurs, the system is located, damage occurs, or the victim resides. Authorizes courts to issue orders to block, blacklist, shut down, or disable harmful uploads or programs. Ensures migrant women and children receive legal, medical, and social services abroad and upon repatriation, including sexual and reproductive health services and anti-sexual assault kits.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08464

Full Title: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE TRAVEL TAX

Short Title: Travel Tax Abolition Act Of 2026

Abstract: Abolishes the travel tax imposed under PD No. 1183, as amended, and Section 73 of RA No. 9593, otherwise known as the “Tourism Act of 2009” as amended. Prohibits the collection of travel tax by any government or private entity upon the law’s effectivity. Mandates immediate refund of previously paid travel taxes for applicable flights. Mandates the National Government to provide necessary funding to TIEZA for tourism development, the Commission on Higher Education for Higher Education Development Fund, and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts for the National Endowment Fund for Culture and the Arts through the annual General Appropriations Act (GAA). Mandates the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) and the Department of Budget and Management to create rules for refunds and transition to GAA funding within 60 days.

Date Filed: 2026-03-11

Significance: NATIONAL

history.fullHistoryText:
HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08476

Republic Act No.: RA12325

Full Title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE TERTIARY EDUCATION SUBSIDY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10931, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO QUALITY TERTIARY EDUCATION ACT”, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Expanding The Coverage Of The Tertiary Education Subsidy, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 10931, Otherwise Known As The “ Universal Access To Quality Tertiary Education Act ”, And Appropriating Funds Therefor



Abstract: Proposes adjustments in the Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) program to ensure that the poorest and most vulnerable households benefit from the program by guaranteeing access to students from households under the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps). Proposes to cover the full cost of tuition and other school fees based on certain conditions. Provides policies in determining allowances and subsidies under TES; Establishes implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance mechanisms to improve the program to make it more responsive to the needs of beneficiaries.

Date Filed: 2026-03-11

Significance: NATIONAL

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08477

Full Title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PRESIDENTIAL MERIT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM,
INTEGRATING THE BAGONG PILIPINAS MERIT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM INTO A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK TO SUPPORT TOP-PERFORMING STUDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Presidential Merit Scholarship Act

Abstract: ims to provide educational support to academically talented Senior High School graduates from families in need of financial assistance; produce a highly competitive and skilled workforce that will address hard-to-fill occupations; and complement existing government scholarship programs by covering academically exceptional students. Requires that a beneficiary student shall be a Filipino citizen or dual citizen residing in the Philippines belonging to top one percent (1%) of the graduating class, has passed the college entrance examination, and has complied with other related requirements for admission in the SUC, LUC, or PHEI, as well as the prescribed requirements of the CHED. Provides other qualification and termination guidelines for PMSP scholarships. Provides tuition subsidy, stipend, other education-related allowances, and Certificate of Presidential Recognition to qualified PMSP scholars. Mandates CHED to create a Presidential Merit Scholarship under the Office of Student Development and Services for program administration, monitoring and evaluation.

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09377

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CIVIC EDUCATION BY INTEGRATING THE STUDY OF THE CONSTITUTION INTO THE CURRICULUM OF BASIC EDUCATION AND INSTITUTIONALIZING THE OBSERVANCE OF CONSTITUTION DAY IN SCHOOLS

Short Title: “ Constitutional Education Act ”



Abstract: Aims to enhance civic education by including the study of the Constitution in early education. Seeks to develop responsible, informed, and patriotic citizens through constitutional literacy. Promotes understanding of governance, rights, duties, and democratic values among students. Mandates the DepEd to integrate constitutional topics from Grade 1 that include history, sovereignty, government branches, rights, citizenship, and local governance, among others. States that all schools shall observe Constitution Day with student-led activities to encourage participatory democracy and deepen learners’ appreciation of constitutional principles and civil engagement. Mandates the DepEd to coordinate with the Supreme Court and Integrated Bar of the Philippines to create teacher training and certification programs.

Date Filed: 2026-05-20

Significance: NATIONAL

Principal Author/s

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09461

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CHILD PROTECTION SAFEGUARDS, REGULATORY MEASURES, POLICIES AND ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS AGAINST ONLINE SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION OF CHILDREN (OSAEC) AND CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION MATERIALS (CSAEM), REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11930, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-ONLINE SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION OF CHILDREN (OSAEC) AND ANTI-CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION MATERIALS (CSAEM) ACT,” PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Child Online Safety And Protection Act Of 2026

Abstract: Seeks to enhance measures against online and offline child sexual abuse and exploitation, and emphasizes a whole-of-government approach, including coordination among agencies and international cooperation. Defines Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Material (CSAEM) as any visual or audio material involving child abuse, whether real or synthetic. Defines Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) as any conduct in information and communication technologies used as an instrument, venue, or means to sexually abuse and/or exploit a child. Covers acts using ICT for production, grooming, luring, extortion, and sexualization of children. Recognizes ICT as a primary instrument in offenses, including creation, distribution, and promotion of CSAEM. Provides duties and responsibilities of entities like ISPs, platform, and device manufacturers to adopt child-protection standards and prevent, detect, and report OSAEC and CSAEM. Promotes children’s rights to safe digital access and aligns with UN and International treaties and prioritizes child welfare, recovery, and survivor participation in law enforcement and policymaking. Penalizes unlawful acts to produce, share, stream, or facilitate CSAEM or related activities, regardless of child’s consent. Penalties range from imprisonment and fines, with hasher sanctions for large-scale or syndicate offenses.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09466

Full Title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE NATIONAL FEEDING PROGRAM INTO A NATIONAL NUTRITION PROGRAM BY EXPANDING ITS SCOPE AND COVERAGE AND ENHANCING ITS SUPPORT MECHANISMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11037, OR THE “MASUSTANSYANG PAGKAIN PARA SA BATANG PILIPINO ACT"

Short Title: Converting The National Feeding Program Into A National Nutrition Program By Expanding Its Scope And Coverage And Enhancing Its Support Mechanisms, And Appropriating Funds Therefor, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11037, Or The “ Masustansyang Pagkain Para Sa Batang Pilipino Act "

Abstract: Establishes the National Nutrition Program to address undernutrition among Filipino children. Implements a school-based feeding initiative for all public school learners from kindergarten to grade 12, with at least one fortified meal for 200 days. It covers supplemental feeding for undernourished children below five years old, health and nutrition services, micronutrient supplementation, and nutrition education. Mandates procurement of produce from small-scale farmers and fisherfolk, prioritizing at least 30% of supplies from local producers. Establishes a registry of small-scale producers and supports farmers through training, subsidies, storage facilities, and access to credit. Mandates the Department of Agriculture, Department of Health, Department of Education, and DSWD to implement and coordinate program components. Establishes a National School Feeding Cloud Kitchen System for efficient meal management.

history.fullHistoryText:
HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09532

Full Title: AN ACT PROVIDING UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO DIGITAL ACADEMIC TEXTBOOKS, LEARNING MATERIALS, AND WIRELESS FIDELITY FOR STUDENTS IN PUBLIC AND PRIVATE HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS THROUGH THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A NATIONAL ACADEMIC CONTENT REPOSITORY

Short Title: “ Universal Access To Digital Academic Learning Resources Act ”.

Abstract: Aims to provide free digital textbooks, learning materials, and high-speed Wi-Fi to students and faculty nationwide. Supports digitization, localization, and sharing of academic content, promoting digital literacy and research. Creates the National Academic Content Repository (NACR) to store and disseminate digital textbooks, lecture videos, research papers, and open educational resources. NACR content shall be quality-assured, accessible, inclusive, and culturally relevant, with faculty-generated contributions encouraged. Requires CHED to acquire licenses, promote local content creation through grants, and collaborate with publishers for affordable or open access. Mandates DICT and HEIs to implement campus-wide free Wi-Fi, prioritizing rural and under-resourced campuses, with secure and monitored access. Offers capacity-building programs that include faculty training, recognition incentives for content creators, and technical assistance for infrastructure.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09812

Full Title: AN ACT PRESCRIBING THE MANDATORY GUIDELINES FOR THE ESTABLISHMENT, OPERATION, AND GOVERNANCE OF LOCAL UNIVERSITIES AND COLLEGES

Short Title: Local Universities And Colleges ( L U Cs ) Governance Act

Abstract: Aims to rationalize, regulate, and standardize the creation, administration, and academic operations of Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs) across the Philippines to ensure quality higher education, financial sustainability, and alignment with local labor market needs. Establishes that local educational institutions created by Local Government Units (LGUs) must obtain the explicit approval of the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) or the Technical Education and Skills Development Authority (TESDA) prior to offering associate degrees, diploma programs, bachelor’s degree programs, or nondegree programs. Programs must fully comply with CHED's Policies, Standards, and Guidelines (PSGs) and TESDA's training standards. Mandates that for an LGU to establish or operate an LUC, it must submit four key documents for review and approval: 1. Feasibility Study; 2. Certification of Availability of Funds 3. Project Development Plan; and 4. Five-Year Institutional Development Plan. States that all LUCs established in accordance with these mandatory guidelines become eligible to avail themselves of benefits under Republic Act No. 10931 or The Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act. Makes compliant LUCs eligible for national government grants, subsidies, and funding support subject to existing guidelines.

Date Filed: 2026-06-08

Significance: NATIONAL

2. ORETA, ANTOLIN III A.

3. RODRIGUEZ, RUFUS B.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB10923

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION OF PATIENTS AGAINST HOSPITAL DETENTION ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES AND PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9439, ENTITLED “AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES”

Short Title: Strengthening The Protection Of Patients Against Hospital Detention On Grounds Of Nonpayment Of Hospital Bills Or Medical Expenses And Providing Stiffer Penalties For Violations Thereof, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 9439, Entitled “ An Act Prohibiting The Detention Of Patients In Hospitals And Medical Clinics On Grounds Of Nonpayment Of Hospital Bills Or Medical Expenses ”

Abstract: Explicitly prohibits hospitals, clinics, and similar facilities from detaining patients, including newborns and deceased persons, once they are medically discharged or have died for reasons of nonpayment in part or full, of hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees. Detention includes, physical restraint, withholding discharge documents, releasing personal belongings, or holding cadavers for nonpayment. The law expands coverage to relatives and caregivers in exchange for allowing patients to leave. Patients discharged or wishing to leave but unable to pay must be allowed to do so, with the right to obtain discharge papers upon executing a promissory note secured by various guarantees. Indigent patients endorsed by the Medical Social Services Office to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the Department of Health are exempt from promissory notes, with the DSWD or DOH guarantees accepted instead. Penalties for violations includes fines and imprisonment, with hasher sanctions for violations committed under hospital policies or management instructions. Repeated violations can lead to license revocation. Requires the Department of Health (DOH) and Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to ensure access to medical assistance to programs for indigent and financially incapacitated patients. Mandates the DOH to establish a grievance and redress mechanism for patients and their families who are unlawfully detained in hospitals, medical clinics, or similar facilities due to non-payment of hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees.

Full Title: AN ACT FIXING THE TERM OF OFFICE OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN TO FIVE (5) YEARS, AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 12232 OR “AN ACT SETTING THE TERM OF OFFICE OF BARANGAY OFFICIALS AND MEMBERS OF THE SANGGUNIANG KABATAAN, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”

Short Title: Fixing The Term Of Office Of Barangay Officials And Members Of The Sangguniang Kabataan To Five (5) Years, Amending Republic Act No. 12232 Or “ An Act Setting The Term Of Office Of Barangay Officials And Members Of The Sangguniang Kabataan, And For Other Purposes ”

Abstract: The bill amends Republic Act No.12232 to set the term of office for barangay and SK Officials at five years. It moves the next elections from the first Monday of November 2026 to Second Monday of November 2028, with subsequent elections every five years. States that incumbent elective officials are considered to have completed one term due to a two-year extension. Officials serving three consecutive terms in the same position become ineligible to run again in 2028. The bill limits the term of office of elected barangay officials to two (2) consecutive terms and one (1) for SK officials.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06276

Full Title: AN ACT INSTITUTING A LOAN RESTRUCTURING AND CONDONATION PROGRAM FOR SOCIALIZED AND LOW-COST HOUSING

Short Title: Housing Loan Condonation Act

Abstract: Aims to make available at affordable cost, decent housing and basic services to underprivileged and homeless citizens. Condones all socialized and low-cost housing loans with the NHA, SHFC, NHMFC, AND PCG that have at least three (3) months of unpaid monthly amortizations for a period of twenty-four (24) months after the issuance of the implementing rules and regulations of this Act, provided, that the original principal amount of the housing loans shall not exceed One million eight hundred thousand pesos (P1,800,00.00). Authorizes the NHA, SHFC, NHMFC, and PGC to continue the loan restructuring and condonation program notwithstanding the lapse of twenty-four months application period. Allows restructuring of housing loans and the assumption of payment of outstanding loan by the legal heirs and successors-in-interest. Provides incentives to all accounts which monthly amortization are paid on time.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09466

Full Title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE NATIONAL FEEDING PROGRAM INTO A NATIONAL NUTRITION PROGRAM BY EXPANDING ITS SCOPE AND COVERAGE AND ENHANCING ITS SUPPORT MECHANISMS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11037, OR THE “MASUSTANSYANG PAGKAIN PARA SA BATANG PILIPINO ACT"

Short Title: Converting The National Feeding Program Into A National Nutrition Program By Expanding Its Scope And Coverage And Enhancing Its Support Mechanisms, And Appropriating Funds Therefor, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 11037, Or The “ Masustansyang Pagkain Para Sa Batang Pilipino Act "

Abstract: Establishes the National Nutrition Program to address undernutrition among Filipino children. Implements a school-based feeding initiative for all public school learners from kindergarten to grade 12, with at least one fortified meal for 200 days. It covers supplemental feeding for undernourished children below five years old, health and nutrition services, micronutrient supplementation, and nutrition education. Mandates procurement of produce from small-scale farmers and fisherfolk, prioritizing at least 30% of supplies from local producers. Establishes a registry of small-scale producers and supports farmers through training, subsidies, storage facilities, and access to credit. Mandates the Department of Agriculture, Department of Health, Department of Education, and DSWD to implement and coordinate program components. Establishes a National School Feeding Cloud Kitchen System for efficient meal management.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08477

Full Title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING THE PRESIDENTIAL MERIT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM,
INTEGRATING THE BAGONG PILIPINAS MERIT SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAM INTO A NATIONAL FRAMEWORK TO SUPPORT TOP-PERFORMING STUDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Presidential Merit Scholarship Act

Abstract: ims to provide educational support to academically talented Senior High School graduates from families in need of financial assistance; produce a highly competitive and skilled workforce that will address hard-to-fill occupations; and complement existing government scholarship programs by covering academically exceptional students. Requires that a beneficiary student shall be a Filipino citizen or dual citizen residing in the Philippines belonging to top one percent (1%) of the graduating class, has passed the college entrance examination, and has complied with other related requirements for admission in the SUC, LUC, or PHEI, as well as the prescribed requirements of the CHED. Provides other qualification and termination guidelines for PMSP scholarships. Provides tuition subsidy, stipend, other education-related allowances, and Certificate of Presidential Recognition to qualified PMSP scholars. Mandates CHED to create a Presidential Merit Scholarship under the Office of Student Development and Services for program administration, monitoring and evaluation.

Date Filed: 2026-03-11

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09461

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CHILD PROTECTION SAFEGUARDS, REGULATORY MEASURES, POLICIES AND ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS AGAINST ONLINE SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION OF CHILDREN (OSAEC) AND CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION MATERIALS (CSAEM), REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11930, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-ONLINE SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION OF CHILDREN (OSAEC) AND ANTI-CHILD SEXUAL ABUSE OR EXPLOITATION MATERIALS (CSAEM) ACT,” PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Child Online Safety And Protection Act Of 2026

Abstract: Seeks to enhance measures against online and offline child sexual abuse and exploitation, and emphasizes a whole-of-government approach, including coordination among agencies and international cooperation. Defines Child Sexual Abuse or Exploitation Material (CSAEM) as any visual or audio material involving child abuse, whether real or synthetic. Defines Online Sexual Abuse or Exploitation of Children (OSAEC) as any conduct in information and communication technologies used as an instrument, venue, or means to sexually abuse and/or exploit a child. Covers acts using ICT for production, grooming, luring, extortion, and sexualization of children. Recognizes ICT as a primary instrument in offenses, including creation, distribution, and promotion of CSAEM. Provides duties and responsibilities of entities like ISPs, platform, and device manufacturers to adopt child-protection standards and prevent, detect, and report OSAEC and CSAEM. Promotes children’s rights to safe digital access and aligns with UN and International treaties and prioritizes child welfare, recovery, and survivor participation in law enforcement and policymaking. Penalizes unlawful acts to produce, share, stream, or facilitate CSAEM or related activities, regardless of child’s consent. Penalties range from imprisonment and fines, with hasher sanctions for large-scale or syndicate offenses.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06739

Full Title: AN ACT CONVERTING THE DR. EVA MACARAEG-MACAPAGAL NATIONAL CENTER FOR GERIATRIC HEALTH UNDER THE JOSE R. REYES MEMORIAL MEDICAL CENTER AS THE DR. EVA MACARAEG-MACAPAGAL NATIONAL CENTER FOR GERIATRIC HEALTH AND RESEARCH INSTITUTE, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Geriatric Health Act

Abstract: Aims to protect and promote the right to health of senior citizens by ensuring holistic health services through the establishment of a geriatric specialty hospital and research institute. Grants the Dr. Eva Macaraeg-Macapagal National Center for Geriatric Health and Research Institute (DEMM-NCGHRI) the function to serve as an apex hospital or end-referral facility which shall specialize in geriatric health services; provide higher and up-to-date geriatric training for professionals, postgraduates, academics and allied healthcare providers especially from the geriatric specialty centers and; conduct cutting edge research studies on diseases related to old age for the development of policies, protocols, standards, and solutions for specialized health care, among others. Provides tax exemptions for all donations, endowments, contributions, grants and bequests used actually, directly and exclusively for and in accordance with the purposes and functions of the DEMM-NCGHRI. Mandates the DEMM-NCGHRI to submit an annual report to the President of the Philippines, the Senate Committee on Health and Demography, and the House of Representatives Committee on Health, on its activities, accomplishments, and recommendations.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09377

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING CIVIC EDUCATION BY INTEGRATING THE STUDY OF THE CONSTITUTION INTO THE CURRICULUM OF BASIC EDUCATION AND INSTITUTIONALIZING THE OBSERVANCE OF CONSTITUTION DAY IN SCHOOLS

Short Title: “ Constitutional Education Act ”



Abstract: Aims to enhance civic education by including the study of the Constitution in early education. Seeks to develop responsible, informed, and patriotic citizens through constitutional literacy. Promotes understanding of governance, rights, duties, and democratic values among students. Mandates the DepEd to integrate constitutional topics from Grade 1 that include history, sovereignty, government branches, rights, citizenship, and local governance, among others. States that all schools shall observe Constitution Day with student-led activities to encourage participatory democracy and deepen learners’ appreciation of constitutional principles and civil engagement. Mandates the DepEd to coordinate with the Supreme Court and Integrated Bar of the Philippines to create teacher training and certification programs.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB06789

Full Title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE NATIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR WATER RESOURCE MANAGEMENT AND CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER RESOURCES AND THE WATER REGULATORY COMMISSION, DEFINING THEIR MANDATES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: National Water Resources Management Act

Abstract: Aims to ensure universal access to safe, affordable, and sustainable water while addressing the challenges of climate change and ecological balance. Creates the Department of Water Resources (DWR) which shall be the primary agency responsible for the comprehensive and integrated identification and mapping of all water resources, planning, policy formulation, and management of the ownership, appropriation, utilization, exploitation, development, and protection of water resources in the Philippines to ensure optimal use thereof. Establishes the Water Regulatory Commission which shall cover and apply to all service providers, whether private or public, providing or intending to provide water supply, including suppliers to subdivisions or other service providers, sewerage, or septage treatment and disposal services for domestic, residential, institutional, industrial or commercial use. Establishes interdepartmental relations with other agencies such as the Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR), Department of Health (DOH), LGUs and the PCC. Promotes “water demand management” as a national policy, encouraging recycling, rainwater harvesting, and efficient pricing to make conservation a way of life. Mandates that a portion (up to 10%) of proceeds from raw water extraction be shared with the Local Government Units (LGUs) or Indigenous Cultural Communities (IPs) that own the land where the water is sourced. Provides the Department and Commission to absorb the relevant functions and rights of existing agencies, such as the National Water Resources Board (NWRB) and the regulatory units of the MWSS and LWUA.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08043

Full Title: AN ACT REDUCING FOOD SURPLUS THROUGH FOOD DONATIONS AND FOOD WASTE RECYCLING

Short Title: Food Waste Reduction And Prevention Act

Abstract: Aims to attain food security, end hunger, promote the efficient use of the country’s food resources, and protect the environment by reducing food waste and its greenhouse gas emissions. Mandates the donation of edible food surplus to accredited food banks. Requires covered establishments to implement food waste prevention plans, reduce surplus at source, and enter into contracts with food banks. Businesses achieving at least 20% reduction in edible surplus are eligible for enhanced tax deductions.

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB05990

Full Title: AN ACT PROVIDING EDUCATION PATHWAYS FOR BASIC EDUCATION STUDENTS, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Abstract: Seeks to restructure the Senior High School program by establishing clear education pathways after Junior High School: 1) University Preparatory Pathway, managed by the DepEd, to prepare learners for college; and 2) the Technical-Vocational Pathway, managed by TESDA, to provide job-ready skills aligned with industry standards. Aims to introduce flexible and inclusive education pathways to give Filipino students genuine choices that reflect strengths, aspirations, and opportunities, while ensuring that basic education remains responsive to social and economic realities. HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08420

Full Title: AN ACT DEFINING TECHNOLOGY-FACILITATED VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN, PROVIDING PROTECTIVE MEASURES, AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9262, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “ANTI-VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND THEIR CHILDREN ACT OF 2004”

Short Title: Expanded Anti - Violence Against Women And Their Children ( E - V A W C ) Act

Abstract: Seeks to define and address electronic violence against women and their children. Broadens the scope to include acts committed or condoned by the state, covering physical, sexual, psychological, and economic abuse. Psychological violence includes coercion to witness abuse, pornography, harm to pets, or deprivation of custody or visitation rights. Defines acts involving data, ICT devices, or digital media causing mental, emotional, sexual, or physical harm. Includes unauthorized recording/distribution of intimate images or videos, cyber harassment, stalking, fake news creation, and malicious social media account use. Imposes penalties of reclusion temporal, fines between P300,000.00 to P500,000.00 and mandatory psychological or psychiatric treatment. Provides Family or Regional Trial Courts the exclusive jurisdiction over VAWC cases. Cases involving technology-facilitated violence against women and their children (TFVAWC) can be filed where the offense occurs, the system is located, damage occurs, or the victim resides. Authorizes courts to issue orders to block, blacklist, shut down, or disable harmful uploads or programs. Ensures migrant women and children receive legal, medical, and social services abroad and upon repatriation, including sexual and reproductive health services and anti-sexual assault kits.

history.fullHistoryText:
HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08476

Republic Act No.: RA12325

Full Title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF THE TERTIARY EDUCATION SUBSIDY, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 10931, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “UNIVERSAL ACCESS TO QUALITY TERTIARY EDUCATION ACT”, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

Short Title: Expanding The Coverage Of The Tertiary Education Subsidy, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 10931, Otherwise Known As The “ Universal Access To Quality Tertiary Education Act ”, And Appropriating Funds Therefor



Abstract: Proposes adjustments in the Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES) program to ensure that the poorest and most vulnerable households benefit from the program by guaranteeing access to students from households under the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps). Proposes to cover the full cost of tuition and other school fees based on certain conditions. Provides policies in determining allowances and subsidies under TES; Establishes implementation, monitoring, and quality assurance mechanisms to improve the program to make it more responsive to the needs of beneficiaries.

Date Filed: 2026-03-11

Significance: NATIONAL

Full Title: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE PROTECTION OF PATIENTS AGAINST HOSPITAL DETENTION ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES AND PROVIDING STIFFER PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9439, ENTITLED “AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DETENTION OF PATIENTS IN HOSPITALS AND MEDICAL CLINICS ON GROUNDS OF NONPAYMENT OF HOSPITAL BILLS OR MEDICAL EXPENSES”

Short Title: Strengthening The Protection Of Patients Against Hospital Detention On Grounds Of Nonpayment Of Hospital Bills Or Medical Expenses And Providing Stiffer Penalties For Violations Thereof, Amending For The Purpose Republic Act No. 9439, Entitled “ An Act Prohibiting The Detention Of Patients In Hospitals And Medical Clinics On Grounds Of Nonpayment Of Hospital Bills Or Medical Expenses ”

Abstract: Explicitly prohibits hospitals, clinics, and similar facilities from detaining patients, including newborns and deceased persons, once they are medically discharged or have died for reasons of nonpayment in part or full, of hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees. Detention includes, physical restraint, withholding discharge documents, releasing personal belongings, or holding cadavers for nonpayment. The law expands coverage to relatives and caregivers in exchange for allowing patients to leave. Patients discharged or wishing to leave but unable to pay must be allowed to do so, with the right to obtain discharge papers upon executing a promissory note secured by various guarantees. Indigent patients endorsed by the Medical Social Services Office to the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) and the Department of Health are exempt from promissory notes, with the DSWD or DOH guarantees accepted instead. Penalties for violations includes fines and imprisonment, with hasher sanctions for violations committed under hospital policies or management instructions. Repeated violations can lead to license revocation. Requires the Department of Health (DOH) and Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) to ensure access to medical assistance to programs for indigent and financially incapacitated patients. Mandates the DOH to establish a grievance and redress mechanism for patients and their families who are unlawfully detained in hospitals, medical clinics, or similar facilities due to non-payment of hospital bills, medical expenses, or professional fees.

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08413

Full Title: AN ACT GRANTING TWENTY PERCENT (20%) DISCOUNT OR EXEMPTION FROM FEES AND CHARGES TO INDIGENT JOB SEEKERS FOR CERTAIN PRE-EMPLOYMENT DOCUMENTS ISSUED BY GOVERNMENT AGENCIES

Short Title: Kabalikat Sa Hanapbuhay Act

Abstract: Establishes a “Kabalikat sa Hanapbuhay Act” to support indigent job seekers by reducing or waiving fees from pre-employment documents. Aims to promote social equity, full employment, and poverty alleviation through accessible government services. Grants indigent job seekers a 20% discount on fees for clearances and certificates such as barangay clearance, NBI clearance, police clearance, medical certificate, certificate of live birth, marriage certificate, national certificate and certificate of competency for TESDA, Civil Service eligibility certificate, and other documentary requirements issued by any government agency that may be required by employers from indigent job seekers. Waives fees for TIN cards and certain education documents from government and local universities. Limits the privilege to waived or discounted fees to once every six (6) months from each government agency. Tasks the Philippine Statistical Authority (PSA) to issue free Certificate of Indigency based on CBMS data. Establishes an Interagency Coordinating and Monitoring Committee to coordinate and monitor the implementation of this Act.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB08464

Full Title: AN ACT ABOLISHING THE TRAVEL TAX

Short Title: Travel Tax Abolition Act Of 2026

Abstract: Abolishes the travel tax imposed under PD No. 1183, as amended, and Section 73 of RA No. 9593, otherwise known as the “Tourism Act of 2009” as amended. Prohibits the collection of travel tax by any government or private entity upon the law’s effectivity. Mandates immediate refund of previously paid travel taxes for applicable flights. Mandates the National Government to provide necessary funding to TIEZA for tourism development, the Commission on Higher Education for Higher Education Development Fund, and the National Commission for Culture and the Arts for the National Endowment Fund for Culture and the Arts through the annual General Appropriations Act (GAA). Mandates the Tourism Infrastructure and Enterprise Zone Authority (TIEZA) and the Department of Budget and Management to create rules for refunds and transition to GAA funding within 60 days.

Date Filed: 2026-03-11

Significance: NATIONAL

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09305

Full Title: AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING A NATIONAL EMERGENCY RESPONSE AND RESILIENCY FRAMEWORK AND GRANTING EMERGENCY P0WERS TO THE PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES, CREATING FOR THE PURPOSE THE "KALINGA PROGRAM" TO ENSURE ECONOMIC STABILITY, ENERGY SECURITY, AND CONTINUITY OF ESSENTIAL SERVICES

Short Title: Komprehensibong Alalay Sa Livelihood, Inflation, Negosyo At Goods Assistance ( K A L I N G A ) Act

Abstract: Aims to institutionalize a national emergency response and resiliency framework and grant temporary emergency powers to the President to manage fuel-driven inflation, secure energy and essential goods supply, and protect vulnerable sectors. Establishes the KALINGA Program, which functions as the government’s core national emergency response framework during periods of extreme fuel price volatility or energy shocks. The program is designed to be targeted, time-bound, data-driven, transparent, fiscally responsible, and subject to congressional oversight. Empowers the President to declare a state of national emergency upon the recommendation of the KALINGA National Response Council if any of the following objective, data-driven metrics are met and certified by the Department of Energy (DOE): • The average Dubai crude oil price based on the Mean of Platts Singapore (MOPS) reaches or exceeds $80 USD per barrel for 30 consecutive days. • The average domestic fuel price increases by at least 30% within a 30-day window. • National fuel inventory levels fall below a 30-day supply. Mandates strict transparency safeguards to prevent aid duplication, fund leakage, and fraud. Furthermore, the emergency powers granted to the President are strictly temporary and will automatically expire once the declaration of national emergency is officially lifted, or when the Council determines the emergency indicators have safely receded.

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09397

Full Title: AN ACT UPHOLDING THE PEOPLE’S CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT TO ACCESS INFORMATION AND PROMOTING FULL PUBLIC DISCLOSURE OF ALL GOVERNMENT TRANSACTIONS INVOLVING PUBLIC INTEREST

Short Title: Right To Information ( R T I ) Act Of 2026

Abstract: Aims to uphold the people’s right to access government information and promote transparency and emphasizes accountability, public participation, and the ethical use of emerging technologies like AI. Applies to all government offices, including executive, legislative, judicial, and local government units, and private entities performing public functions or using public funds. Establishes an independent, quasi-judicial body called the RTI Commission which shall be responsible for implementing laws, setting standards, settling disputes, and providing guidance. Sets the composition and appointment of the RTI Commission

Significance: NATIONAL

HOUSE BILL/RESOLUTION HISTORY

Congress: 20th Congress

House Bill/Resolution No.: HB09465

Full Title: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE DELIBERATE DISSEMINATION OF FALSE INFORMATION THAT POSES VERIFIABLE PUBLIC HARM OR SERIOUS THREAT TO NATIONAL SECURITY, ESTABLISHING DIGITAL PLATFORM ACCOUNTABILITY AND TRANSPARENCY MECHANISMS, AND PROMOTING MEDIA AND DIGITAL LITERACY

Short Title: Digital Media Anti - False Information Act

Abstract: Aims to criminalize and regulate the dissemination of false information and fake news that harms the public or threatens security through digital media in the Philippines. Mandates all digital platforms to establish local legal entities, disclose sponsored content, submit annual transparency reports, maintain ad repositories, ensure transparency algorithms, and avoid manipulative interface designs, among others. Mandates large platforms designated as VLP-PH to conduct risk assessments, undergo annual audits, and appoint compliance officers. They must also provide data access for research, implement risk mitigation plans, and engage with third-party fact-checking organizations in providing context, labeling, or verification, and with academic, professional, and civil society organizations to promote media and information literacy. Penalizes violators to face imprisonment from 6 to 12 years and fines from Five hundred thousand pesos up to 2 million pesos, or both. Exempts political opinions, criticism of government, criticism of public officials or candidates, satire, journalistic inquiry, investigative reporting, editorial judgement, whistleblowing, public interest advocacy, commentary, opinion, academic discourse, artistic and religious expression, and other forms of protected speech. Directs the Department of Education and CHED to integrate media literacy into curricula emphasizing critical thinking and fact-checking, and all national government agencies and local government units to maintain open data portals containing verifiable public information. Mandates the Department of Information and Communications Technology to develop the implementing rules and regulations in consultation with stakeholders.
